claims.claim: (a1) apps/moderation-worker/tests/moderation-stats-contract.test.ts fails on preview/integration-2026-10-04, and only because of the #224 comment at apps/presets-api/src/handlers/moderation.ts:390.
claims.evidence: The single-test run fails 1 of 2: 'declares exactly the keys presets-api returns' at :57, with exactly one extra alias, "the". The '_count' test passes. The test's regex is /SELECT\b([\s\S]*?as\s+actions_last_week)/i, so its span starts at the file's first SELECT. That is the INSERT…SELECT at line 225, not the stats query at 479; the test docblock's 'anchored to the statement' claim is weaker than it reads. Scanning the span (lines 225-484) with /\bas\s+([a-z_]+)/gi gives 390 'as the', then 480-484 pending, approved, rejected, flagged, actions_last_week. Nothing else in the span matches. Lines 129, 133 and 201 contain 'as …' but sit before line 225. gates-before.txt agrees: Tasks 61 successful, 62 total; moderation-worker 1 failed, 762 passed (763).

claims.claim: (a2) Rewording that comment alone makes the test pass, and no other text in the span would match.
claims.evidence: I replaced line 390 in memory only, with no file written. Both '  // review writes neither (mirrors the revert route above).' and '…(same shape that the revert route above uses).' then yield exactly [actions_last_week, approved, flagged, pending, rejected], which equals Object.keys(declared). Two hazards for any future rewording: (1) the regex is case-insensitive, so 'As foo' also matches; (2) \s+ crosses newlines, so a comment line ending in 'as' would capture the first identifier on the next line (here 'const').

claims.claim: (b1) discord-worker's /preset submit and /preset edit moderation notifications omit contentRevision, while the webhook path passes it.
claims.evidence: Line 576 calls notifyModerationChannel, which at 1137-1150 passes {kind:'new', preset, categoryName}. Line 924 calls notifyEditModerationChannel, which at 1156-1172 passes {kind:'edit', preset, original, categoryName}. Neither passes contentRevision. The webhook path at apps/discord-worker/src/index.ts:404-409 passes contentRevision: preset.content_revision. claims.claim: (b2) presets-api 2.4.0 submit/edit responses include content_revision in the object discord-worker receives.
claims.evidence:
They do not.
- Submit: the response is presetForViewer(preset), where preset is createPreset's literal object (preset-service.ts:420ff), which has no content_revision.
- Edit: the response is presetForViewer(updatedPreset), where updatedPreset = updatePreset → rowToPreset (preset-service.ts:721). rowToPreset (52-129) does not map content_revision.
- toPublicPreset returns the preset unchanged for authSource 'bot' (preset-service.ts:173-175), so it adds nothing.
- packages/types/src has no content_revision, so CommunityPreset cannot carry it.
- presets.ts:836-840 notes that RETURNING * does not see the AFTER-trigger bump, so even a raw RETURNING value would be stale.
- apps/presets-api/CLAUDE.md says the token is intentionally omitted from public responses.
- Only the webhook payloads add it, after a fresh re-read: presets.ts:853 (edit) and :1081 (submit).
So the direct /preset paths have no revision they could pass.

claims.claim: (b3) Sprint 0 observation headline: bot-submitted presets get legacy moderation buttons.
claims.evidence: True of the embed discord-worker posts itself, but incomplete. presets-api also fires the webhook for bot-sourced submits and edits: notifyDiscordBot at presets.ts ~1068-1090 and ~846-878 has no authSource filter, and DISCORD_WORKER is bound in both wrangler.toml blocks. discord-worker's webhook (index.ts:402) gates only on status === 'pending'. So a pending bot submission or flagged edit gets two moderation embeds: a revision-bound one from the webhook (Source: Discord) and a legacy-id one from preset.ts. This dual post already exists on main (both paths present at 8ecb878f); #227 did not introduce it. The practical remedy is to drop or merge the duplicate direct post, not to plumb a revision, which the response does not carry.
